newsitem.title: USA: Michigan ends fiscal 1996 with $88.1 mln surplus.
newsitem.headline: Michigan ends fiscal 1996 with $88.1 mln surplus.

text.p: Michigan ended fiscal 1996 with a $88.1 million budget surplus, according to the preliminary results of the state's fiscal year book-closing released to the legislature Monday.

Just over $58 million of the surplus for the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30 will be deposited into the state's budget stabilization fund. That deposit will bring the fund's balance to more than $1.1 billion -- representing 7.3 percent of Michigan's combined general fund, the state's department of management and budget said in a news release.
The remaining $30 million of the surplus will be used for capital projects at state arts and cultural facilities, airport projects and special maintenance and remodeling needs.
Gov. John Engler said the surplus was a "direct result of Michigan's dramatically improved economic climate and strong, disciplined fiscal management."

The surplus, which was smaller than the $112.1 million balance recorded by the state for fiscal 1995 and the $464 million surplus in fiscal 1994, marked the fourth consecutive year that state departments avoided overspending in their appropriated budgets, the release said.
A final determination of Michigan's fiscal 1996 surplus is scheduled to be released in March.
